subject: Eval go/no-go criteria & CV sampling for Acme POC
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Eval go/no-go criteria & CV sampling: Acme POC

Team —

Quick ask to align before the Acme POC kickoff (next week). Product wants a crisp acceptance checklist and sampling plan we can hand to the SRE/release team so they can gate the rollout automatically. High-level asks below; fill in specifics and call out any blockers.

Goals:
- Define go/no-go thresholds for the A/B (model A = current, model B = release candidate).
- Specify sample sizes and slice definitions (CV sampling) for automated evaluation and for the manual QA batch.
- Define rollback/exception criteria and an operations contact chain.

Initial constraints from Acme (they asked us to keep the first canary small):
- 10% traffic canary for 48 hours, then 50% if metrics look good.
- They will require a final sign-off from their analytics team before 100% ramp.

Please respond with concrete numeric thresholds (not just high-level statements). I attached a starter acceptance_matrix.csv and a sketch of a cv_sampling_plan.md — use/edit.

Marissa
Director, Product — Redwood Inference

Attachments: acceptance_matrix.csv (starter), cv_sampling_plan.md (sketch)

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-17T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval go/no-go criteria & CV sampling: Acme POC

Thanks Marissa — I populated the acceptance matrix and sketched a concrete sampling plan. TL;DR proposal below; full details in the attached CSV/MD.

Proposed acceptance gates (A/B compare):
- N (minimum sample for primary metrics): 5,000 labeled interactions per arm for the manual QA batch (stratified by customer segment).
- Topline truthfulness (binary-labeled): no more than 1.0 percentage point absolute drop vs baseline (model A) with p<0.05 (two-sided).
- Hallucination rate (domain-specific definitions, see csv): < 1.5% absolute. If >1.5% or +0.5% vs baseline, fail.
- Latency: median p95 token latency increase <= 10ms per token; p99 latency must remain under 600ms for 8k context.
- Conversion proxy (Acme metric): live A/B must not show >1.5% relative drop in conversion rate during canary (stat sig using sequential test), else automatic rollback.

CV sampling plan highlights:
- Stratified slices: new users, power users, long-context (>=4 turns), sensitive intents (payment, refunds).
- For long-tail intents we will add a focused sample of 500 interactions per slice to ensure coverage.
- Labeling QC: expect 3 annotators per item; IAA threshold 0.75 Fleiss.

Canary rollout automation:
- Phase 1: 10% for 48h. Automated checks run every 6h. If any critical gate trips, traffic reverts to 0% and page is alerted.
- Phase 2: 50% for 24h with expanded telemetry. Manual sign-off required from product for 100% ramp.

Open technical caveats: quantized 8-bit model variant may shift hallucination profile — engineering should ensure the eval harness uses the exact serving runtime configuration to match production.

Olga
Senior PM, Eval & Quality — Redwood Inference

Attachments: acceptance_matrix.csv, cv_sampling_plan.md

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-18T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval go/no-go criteria & CV sampling: Acme POC

+1 to Olga's numbers. A few engineering considerations that affect the acceptance automation and sampling: 

- Runtime parity: we must run the eval harness on the same kernel selection / quantization mode as the canary to avoid false positives. If the canary uses int8 kernels, labelers should evaluate samples produced by that variant.
- Batching and cache effects: traffic profile in canary (10% isolated sessions) can change batching characteristics; include a synthetic burst test in the CV plan (100 concurrent sessions for 15 minutes) and measure p95/p99.
- Drifted prompts: add a holdout of 1,000 production prompts from the last 7 days to detect prompt-distribution drift that might not appear in stratified sampling.
- Automation hooks: we can wire the gate checks into the rollout controller. Need owners for the rule: engineering for latency, research for hallucination labeling QC, product for conversion sign-off.

I'll attach a short script (in the repo) to re-run the sampling plan with the production runtime; request to QA to use it.

Karthik
Principal Engineer — Serving Runtime

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-18T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval go/no-go criteria & CV sampling: Acme POC

Thanks for the clear draft. From the research / labeling side I propose the following additions to make the gate defensible and repeatable: 

- Labeling rubric: add concrete examples for "hallucination" vs "plausible-but-wrong"; include edge-case templates. We'll version the rubric and pin to the eval run.
- Inter-annotator agreement (IAA): require Fleiss kappa >= 0.7 for the manual batch; if below, expand label pool and re-label.
- Semantic-fidelity score: aggregate a 3-point scale (Correct / Partially correct / Incorrect) and compute weighted loss; fail if weighted loss increases by >0.7% absolute vs baseline.
- Early-warning rule: if any slice shows >0.8pp regression on truthfulness with N>=200 in that slice, halt the ramp and create an async triage ticket to the eval channel.

Operational playbook (short):
- Gate fail -> automatic rollback to previous model, create ticket, notify product + engineering + research (owners will be on the ticket).
- Exception path: if fail is due to an instrumentation mismatch (e.g., wrong runtime flags), engineering can request a 1-hour hold for re-eval; product must approve.

I'll prepare a short checklist for the labeling vendor and a template triage ticket.

Soojin
Lead, Applied ML — Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmeretail.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: jon.park@merchantco.com
Date: 2027-05-19T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval go/no-go criteria & CV sampling: Acme POC

Marissa / Olga — thanks for the thorough plan. A few notes from Acme analytics and legal: 

- Acme can accept the 10% / 48h canary but we must be able to revert instantly if conversion drops beyond 1.0% (they will measure conversion in their analytics window). Please make the rollback path explicit and testable.
- Procurement asks for the acceptance matrix and sampling plan as a delivered artifact we can sign off on before Phase 1.
- On labeling: our analytics team will want access to the manual QA batch results (anonymized). Can you add a delivery schedule (ETA for labeled batch)?

If you can share the finalized CSV/MD by EOD Tuesday (2027-05-20), Acme will be ready to sign and we can proceed with the integration next week.

Sarah Liu
Head of Product Analytics — Acme Retail
